sections.chapter_title: Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller
sections.text_helper: Section 48.8.1 "DMA interrupts" in chapter 48 (Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller), RM0522 Rev 1, page 2229.
sections.section_content:
Interrupt registers description
The ETH_DMAC0SR: Channel 0 status register (see Channel 0 status register
(ETH_DMAC0SR)) captures all the interrupt events of that TxDMA and RxDMA channel.
The ETH_DMAC0IER: Channel 0 interrupt enable register (see Channel 0 interrupt enable
register (ETH_DMAC0IER)) contains the corresponding enable bits for each of the interrupt
event.
There are two groups of interrupts in the DMA channel namely Normal and Abnormal
interrupts.They are indicated by Bits[15:14] of ETH_DMAC0SR register respectively. The
normal group is for events that happen during the normal transfer of packets (TI: transmit
interrupt, RI: receive interrupt, TBU: Transmit buffer unavailable) while the abnormal
interrupt events are for error events.
Interrupts are not queued. If the same interrupt event occurs again before the driver
responds to the previous one, no additional interrupts are generated. An interrupt is
generated only once for multiple events. The driver must scan the Interrupt status register
(ETH_DMAISR) for the cause of the interrupt and clear the source in the respective Status
register. The interrupt is cleared only when all the bits of Interrupt status register
(ETH_DMAISR) are cleared.
Receive idle timer
The Receive DMA provides multiple options to generate and regulate the occurrence of a
Receive interrupt (RI) in the Channel 0 status register (ETH_DMAC0SR), after an ingress
packet is transferred to the host memory.
Among these is an option to generate an RI event when the Receive DMA receives and
transfers a receive packet after a long gap or time interval.
The option is enabled by writing a nonzero value to the ITW[4:0] bitfield of theChannel 0 Rx
interrupt watchdog timer register (ETH_DMAC0RXIWTR). The time interval depends on the
programming of this bitfield.
When the option is enabled, this timer restarts when an RI event occurs for which the
following apply:
• The RIE bit is set and the RI status bit is cleared.
• The RI status bit is cleared and RIE is programmed.
Equally, the timer stops and is cleared, and no further action is taken if a new packet is
received before the timer expiry due.
If the timer expires before the next Receive packet is completely transferred to the host
memory, then an RI event is logged and the interrupt is asserted irrespective of the setting
of the IOC bit. The other timers in the Channel 0 Rx interrupt watchdog timer register
(ETH_DMAC0RXIWTR) continue to operate as specified. The timer starts only after a
packet is transferred without a corresponding RI event.
For programming guidelines on the Receive idle timer, see Section48.9.16: Programming
guidelines for receive idle and receive interrupt watchdog timers
Descriptor refetch when the OWN bit is cleared
By default, the DMA engine checks the OWN bit (xDES3[31]) of the descriptor to confirm
whether the descriptor content is valid and can be processed. If the OWN bit is cleared, it
drops the descriptor.
If, however, bit 26 of the Channel 0 control register (ETH_DMAC0CR) is set, the automatic
refetch operation is enabled. In this case, when the DMA engine determines that the OWN
bit is cleared, it attempts to refetch the same descriptor. If the OWN bit is still cleared, the
DMA engine enters Suspend mode and waits for the software to wake it up by writing into or
by updating the tail pointer register, which generates the xBU interrupt.
The description refetch operation may also be required to ensure that the synchronization of
the descriptor field update by the application does not generate any error.
For programming guidelines on the descriptor refetch, see Programming guidelines for
descriptor refetch when the OWN bit is cleared.
Periodic scheduling of transmit and receive interrupt
It is not preferable to generate interrupts for every packet transferred by DMA (RI and TI) for
system throughput performance reasons. The Ethernet peripheral gives the flexibility to
schedule the interrupt at regular intervals using two methods:
1. Set Interrupt on Completion bit in Transmit descriptor (TDES2[31] in Table541: TDES2
normal descriptor (read format)) once for every “required” number of packets to be
transmitted.
2. Similarly, set the IOC (RDES3[30] inTable554: RDES3 normal descriptor (read
format)) bit only at some specific intervals of Receive descriptors. This way, whenever
a received packet transfer to system memory is complete and any of the descriptors
used for that packet transfer has the IOC bit set, only then the RI event is generated.
In addition to above, an interrupt timer called Channel 0 Rx interrupt watchdog timer register
(ETH_DMAC0RXIWTR) is given for flexible control and periodic scheduling of the receive
interrupt. When this interrupt timer is programmed with a nonzero value, it gets activated as
soon as the Rx DMA completes a transfer of a received packet to system memory without
asserting the Receive interrupt because the corresponding interrupt of completion IOC bit
(RDES3[30] inTable554: RDES3 normal descriptor (read format)) is not set. When this
timer runs out as per the programmed value, RI bit is set and the interrupt is asserted if the
corresponding RIE is enabled in ETH_DMAC0IER register (see Channel 0 interrupt enable
register (ETH_DMAC0IER)). The timer is stopped and cleared before it expires, if the RI is
set for a packet transfer whose descriptor’s IOC was set. The timer is reactivated
automatically after the next packet transfer is complete without the RI event being
generated.
Receive interrupt watchdog timer
When the DMA channel receives a packet and an SOP is detected, an internal timer starts.
This timer accumulates the packet size extracted from the received packet status
(expressed in bytes) over the number of packets received, starting with the packet for which
the Receive DMA does not assert the Receive interrupt (RI) because the corresponding
interrupt of completion (IOC), namely the DES3[30]bit, is not set.
When the number of accumulated bytes per packet equals or exceeds the programmed
value, if the corresponding RIE is enabled in the Channel 0 interrupt enable register
(ETH_DMAC0IER), then the RI bit is set and the interrupt is asserted.
If the RI bit is set for a packet transfer whose descriptor IOC was set, or if the interrupt timer
expires, the timer is stopped and cleared. The timer is reactivated automatically after the
next packet transfer for which the RI event is not generated is complete.
For programming guidelines on the Receive interrupt watchdog timer, see Section48.9.16:
Programming guidelines for receive idle and receive interrupt watchdog timers.
Channel transfer complete interrupt
The transmit transfer complete interrupt (TI) and receive transfer complete interrupt (RI) is
reflected in the channel status register (Channel 0 status register (ETH_DMAC0SR)). The
TI bit is set whenever the Tx DMA channel closes the descriptor in which the IOC bit is set
(Interrupt On Completion - TDES2[31]). Similarly, the RI bit is set whenever the Rx DMA
channel closes the descriptor with the LD bit set and, in any of the descriptors used for
transferring that packet, IOC bit is set (Interrupt Enable on completion - RDES3[30])).
The interrupt signal is asserted for the Transfer complete interrupts only when the
corresponding interrupts are enabled in the channel interrupt enable register (Channel 0
interrupt enable register (ETH_DMAC0IER)).
The behavior of the RI/TI interrupts changes depending on the settings of INTM field
(bits[17:16]) in the ETH_DMAMR register (DMA mode register (ETH_DMAMR)). Table538
explains the behavior of the Transfer Complete interrupt.
